flows.title: High-level diagram
flows.lead: The API inspects and authorizes SQL before isolated execution. It retains a bounded result so later pages do not rerun the query.
flows.heading: Run SQL once. Browse the saved result.

lanes.title: Submit a query
lanes.caption: The initial response already includes a page and a result ID. Reference-free expressions need no published dataset files.

steps.title: Submit SQL
steps.text: Verify the session and browser mutation protection.

steps.title: Inspect the request
steps.text: Identify referenced datasets and reject unsupported SQL within resource limits.

steps.title: Authorize and prepare
steps.text: Authorize every referenced grain, reserve capacity and pin one published generation.

steps.title: Execute unchanged SQL
steps.text: Read approved files only and produce bounded output.

steps.title: Retain and return
steps.text: Confirm worker termination, retain the result and return an authorized page with its ID.

lanes.title: Read another result page
lanes.caption: This path uses saved rows; it does not start a SQL execution or select a newer generation.

steps.title: Choose a result page
steps.text: Send the result ID, page number and session.

steps.title: Check ownership and access
steps.text: Require a live result belonging to the user and recheck access to its datasets.

steps.title: Read the saved slice
steps.text: Use the original page size and stable retained-row boundaries.

steps.title: Return the page
steps.text: Return rows from the same execution with pagination metadata.

boundaries: The parser and query engine run outside the API process with bounded resources.
PostgreSQL owns application access and publication. Query IDs and retained output have a bounded, process-owned lifetime.
Expired or missing results are reported as unavailable; the application does not silently rerun the SQL.
